summary: 86-year-old woman, day 2 after laparotomy for adhesional obstruction: drowsy, inattentive, fluctuating (4AT 8), on morphine PCA and cyclizine, no urine since catheter removal, SpO₂ 93%.

inputs.hpi: Day 2 after laparotomy and adhesiolysis for adhesional small-bowel obstruction. Daughter says she is 'not herself' — sleepy, muddled, not following conversation, worse in the evenings. Pulled out her cannula. Morphine PCA and regular cyclizine. Catheter removed yesterday; not passed urine since. No bowel movement. Previously independent, mild hearing impairment, no known dementia.

exam.general: Drowsy, rousable, inattentive (4AT 8). HR 96, BP 134/70, RR 16, SpO2 93% on air, T 37.4°C.
exam.abdomen: Wound clean. Soft, appropriately tender. Palpable bladder.
exam.respiratory: Reduced air entry at the bases.
exam.neuro: No focal neurology. Pupils pinpoint-small but reactive.

inputs.socialHistory: Widow, lives alone, independent. Hearing aid at home.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Hypoactive post-operative delirium
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Hypoactive delirium day 2 (4AT 8). Likely contributors: opioid PCA, cyclizine (anticholinergic), urinary retention, constipation, hypoxaemia, hyponatraemia. Treat causes, non-pharmacological measures; avoid benzodiazepines.

mustExclude.note: Benzodiazepines worsen delirium; not used except in alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal.
No generalised peritonitis or perforation: an emergency-laparotomy consent line is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: NICE CG103 — Delirium: prevention, diagnosis and management in hospital and long-term care
guideline.section: Identify and manage underlying causes (infection, hypoxia, dehydration, pain, urinary retention, constipation, medication including opioids and anticholinergics); non-pharmacological measures first; short-term antipsychotic only if distressed or a risk to self/others; multicomponent prevention for people at risk (age ≥65, cognitive impairment)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Delirium (CG103). London: NICE; 2010 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: SIGN 157 — Risk reduction and management of delirium
guideline.section: Use the 4AT to detect delirium; benzodiazepines should not be used routinely except in alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal
guideline.citation: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. Risk reduction and management of delirium (SIGN 157). Edinburgh: SIGN; 2019.

rationale: Base post-operative delirium (hypoactive, the form most often missed). Tests the delirium flag, precipitant screen (retention, opioids, anticholinergics, hypoxia, sodium), non-pharmacological care and avoiding benzodiazepines.
